title: Human-readable sizes with iota
hints: Inside a const block, iota counts 0, 1, 2, … for each line, and a line with no expression repeats the previous expression with the next iota.
1 << (10 * iota) gives 1, 1024, 1048576, … Skip the first value with `_ = iota`. To print one decimal place, use fmt.Sprintf("%.1f KB", float64(n)/KB).
const ( _ = iota; KB = 1 << (10 * iota); MB; GB ). Then check the largest unit first: if n >= GB …, else if n >= MB …, else if n >= KB …, else "%d B".
